ai.description: Pillai's Night Frog is a small, 25–30 mm amphibian. It is brown with a distinct pale mid-dorsal stripe and features prominent, expanded toe discs and a snout that projects beyond the lower jaw.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Nyctibatrachus pillaii* is best distinguished by its distinctively pointed, snout-like projection at the tip of the head, which is more pronounced than in similar species.
ai.habitat: *Nyctibatrachus pillaii* inhabits the wet evergreen forests of the southern Western Ghats, typically found near streams at mid-to-high altitudes ranging from 800 to 1,200 meters.
ai.behavior: Pillai's Night Frog is strictly nocturnal, remaining hidden in rock crevices or under leaf litter during the day to avoid predators and desiccation.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Nyctibatrachus pillaii* breeds during the monsoon, laying small clutches of large, unpigmented eggs on wet rocks or vegetation near streams for direct development.
ai.distributionRemarks: Nyctibatrachus pillaii is endemic to the southern Western Ghats in Kerala, India, typically inhabiting high-elevation evergreen forests.
ai.callDescription: Pillai's Night Frog emits a series of high-pitched, insect-like chirps from within dense, wet leaf litter near fast-flowing streams in the Western Ghats.
